title: Scheme-level generic splitting of a finite morphism
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian affine scheme and $g:Z\to S$ a finite morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There is a dense open $U$ of $S$ such that for every open $V\subseteq U$ there is a finite etale surjective morphism $p:T\to V$. On the fibre product $P=Z\times_S T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], using $T\to V\to S$, there are finitely many opens $W_i$ ($i\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$) with union $P$ and pairwise disjoint underlying opens. Each composite $W_i\to P\to T$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. No sheaf occurs in the choice of $U$. The number $n$ may be zero.

source.place: ## Proof, finite-algebra calculation and final paragraph

proof.text: Finite morphisms are affine. Write S=Spec A and Z=Spec B. A is a Noetherian domain and B is finite over A. The generic finite-algebra splitting gives a nonzero c, an etale surjective finite cover Spec A-prime of D(c), and a product decomposition of the reduction of B tensor A-prime into finite universal-homeomorphism factors.

The factor spectra give a finite disjoint open-and-closed decomposition of the reduced source. The reduction is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces; lift the components to the unreduced source. Their maps to the cover are integral, surjective and universally injective since these properties are unchanged by a surjective closed reduction immersion. Hence they are universal homeomorphisms.

For V contained in D(c), base change the cover and the open components. Etaleness, finiteness and surjectivity persist; so do universal homeomorphisms. Opens, disjointness and the covering property persist under this restriction. If the source is empty, take n=0. D(c) is dense because c is nonzero in a domain.

lean.statement: theorem exists_dense_open_finite_scheme_splitting (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral S] [IsNoetherian S] [IsAffine S] {Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Z ⟶ S) [IsFinite g] : ∃ U : S.Opens, Dense (U : Set S) ∧ ∀ (V : S.Opens), V ≤ U → ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (p : T ⟶ V.toScheme), IsFinite p ∧ Etale p ∧ Surjective p ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (W : Fin n → (pullback g (p ≫ V.ι)).Opens), (⨆ i, W i) = ⊤ ∧ Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (W i) (W j)) ∧ ∀ i, IsUniversalHomeomorphism ((W i).ι ≫ pullback.snd g (p ≫ V.ι))
